summary: Famous Indian consumer brands like Parle-G and Maggi generated the highest view counts, while technical corporate tax cases and theoretical economics failed to hold audience interest. Strong numerical hooks paired with iconic daily products consistently outperform abstract financial topics. Going forward, the channel will double down on high-nostalgia Indian brand stories and surprising daily cash facts while strictly eliminating duplicate uploads.
do_more: Focus on mega Indian consumer brands like Parle-G, Maggi, Bisleri, and Nirma that viewers recognize instantly.
Put specific rupee figures and famous brand names in the first 2 seconds of both the script and title.
Structure scripts around a clear conflict like zero-ad marketing hacks, price wars, or comeback stories.
Ensure every script ends with a clean sentence that loops seamlessly back into the opening hook.
avoid: Avoid dry tax court cases like Vicco legal battles that lack mass relatable appeal.
Avoid re-uploading duplicate Shorts or identical scripts, which damages algorithm reach.
Avoid abstract foreign financial stories like hyperinflation without a direct Indian context.
Avoid vague titles that fail to name the brand or specific financial number clearly.
hook_tips: Start with an iconic brand showdown: 'Nirma ne akele Surf Excel ki monopoly kaise khatam ki?'
Lead with daily currency surprises: '₹500 ke note ko chhapne me RBI ka kitna kharcha aata hai?'
Highlight huge financial growth numbers: '₹10 ke popcorn se ₹226 Crore ki empire kaise bani?'
Open with a high-stakes brand question: '1977 me Coca-Cola India se kyu bhaagi aur Thums Up kaise bani?'
title_tips: Pair legendary brands with exact crore metrics: 'Maggi Kaise Bani ₹5000 Crore Brand? 😱 #Shorts'
Ask intriguing daily money questions: '₹500 Note Banane Me Kitna Kharcha Aata Hai? 💵 #Shorts'
